post.title: Brand DNA Explorer
post.hook: Type a website, get its brand as a social feed you can scroll.
post.summary: A Next.js app that presents a brand's colors, voice and imagery as an Instagram style feed, media library and profile. It runs on mock data with a planned analyze endpoint.
post.writeup:
## What it is
Brand DNA is a dark, peach-accented Next.js app that turns a website's brand into something you browse like a social app. Four views: the feed, a media library, a brand profile and saved items. The page title reads "A whole world behind every brand."

## Why
Brand guidelines are usually static PDFs. This prototype explores whether colors, tone of voice, values and imagery feel more alive as posts, stories and a cinematic gallery.

## How it works
The home page starts on mock data for vercel.com. When you enter a domain, the client normalizes the URL, validates it, and POSTs to `/api/analyze-brand`. The response replaces the brand data and the view remounts keyed on the URL. Example brands in the UI are Vercel, Stripe, GitHub and Apple.

The feed has All, Insights and Visuals filters, per post feedback ("Feels right", "Needs work", "Not sure"), and a source dialog. An Instagram style stories component reads colors from the brand palette to theme each story. The media library sorts images into imagery, product and inspiration shelves with an expandable viewer.

The hero artwork was generated from a written prompt: smoky translucent glass and liquid chrome ribbon, peach edges, near-black background, with the left third left clear for text.

## Stack
Next.js, React, Tailwind CSS 4, Radix primitives, Recharts, Zod and the AI SDK. The folder holds 123 files, mostly TypeScript at 83.6%.

## Open questions
The analyze route is called but not among the provided files, so live brand extraction is unverified. There is no git history, so the build order is unknown.
